tasks.short: Review the student's plan and progress, meet mainstream teachers, care coordinator and parents, decide the placement and support, write the placement plan, share it with the mainstream teacher, and schedule class hours and support staff.

steps.what: Special education teacher reviews the student's plan and progress to judge readiness for mainstream classes
Special education teacher meets mainstream teachers, the care coordinator and parents about the placement
Special education teacher decides the placement and support arrangements
Special education teacher coordinates the class hours and support staff in a spreadsheet
Special education teacher writes the placement plan with support arrangements
Special education teacher e-mails the placement plan to the mainstream teacher

tasks.design: The pupil record system ({OTHER}) shows the student's plan goals and progress on one screen, so readiness is judged without leafing through files. The placement plan is a form in the plan module with support arrangements as fields, and the school timetable tool ({PROJECT}) books class hours and support staff. Once written, the plan is shared with the mainstream teacher inside the pupil record system, not by e-mail. Meeting, deciding and support arrangements stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress sat in several files and plans went around as e-mail attachments.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch pupil record systems hold plans, goals and progress with sharing between staff.
tasks.still_hard: Mainstream teachers have full classes and little time for extra support.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a student is ready, even if the scores say not yet.

reach.learn: Whether support arrangements are clear from day one.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records, a development plan module and learning-goal tracking.
Support needs in a plan are health data; a DPIA comes before new pupil-data systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student file to the placement timetable and plan shared; teaching in the mainstream class is outside.
Input contract: plans and progress in the pupil record system; fallback is paper files.
Meetings and decisions do not change.
research_questions: Do placements last longer when plans are shared on time?

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps support fields current.

approvals.approved_version: The placement plan as written by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one placement a term; high: many students moving between classes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the plan meeting, gather test results and specialists' reports, confer with parents and professionals, write the individual plan, check it with parents, and record it with the yearly evaluation date.

steps.what: Special education teacher plans the meeting with parents and professionals by e-mail
Special education teacher gathers test results and reports from specialists
Special education teacher confers with parents, testing specialists and social workers to develop individual educational plans
Special education teacher writes the individual plan
Special education teacher checks the final plan with the parents
Special education teacher records the plan in the pupil administration with the yearly evaluation date

tasks.design: The plan module of the pupil record system ({OTHER}) holds the plan as fields, prefilled with test results, earlier goals and specialists' reports, and runs the legal deadlines (six weeks after enrolment, yearly evaluation) as timers. The meeting is planned with a scheduling poll ({CALENDAR}). Conferring with parents and professionals and writing the plan's goals stay with the teacher; no software writes the plan. Once agreed with the parents, the plan is recorded and the evaluation date set.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were collected by e-mail and plans written in separate documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Plan modules in Dutch pupil record systems hold plans and deadlines.
tasks.still_hard: Parents and professionals rarely agree from the start.
tasks.human_edge: Building a plan that parents feel is about their child, not a form.

reach.learn: Whether plans meet the legal deadlines.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys has a development plan module and learning-goal tracking.
The plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and evaluated yearly.

assumptions: Boundary: from the plan due to the plan recorded; the support itself is outside.
Input contract: test results and reports in the pupil record system; fallback is e-mail and separate documents.
Conferring and writing goals do not change.
Parents' and professionals' time does not change.
research_questions: Do plans meet the six-week deadline more often?

incremental.description: Special education teacher checks prefilled reports are the latest.

approvals.approved_version: The plan as agreed with the parents in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a plan update with few reports; high: a new plan with many specialists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write lesson objectives from core goals and plan goals, adapt them to each student's level, put them on the lesson slides, and explain them to students.

steps.what: Special education teacher writes clear objectives for lessons, units and projects

loop.input: The core goals list, the group plan and the week's lesson topics.
loop.output: Draft objectives per lesson in pupil-friendly language.
loop.check: Code checks every objective maps to a core goal code in the fixed list; objectives without a code are dropped; the teacher edits and approves.
loop.stop: One draft per week; if the teacher rejects it, they write the objectives.
loop.why_not_simpler: A goal list holds formal goals; turning them into lesson-level, pupil-friendly objectives needs prose.

steps.what: Special education teacher adapts objectives to each student's level
Special education teacher puts the objectives on the lesson slides
Special education teacher communicates the objectives to students

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts the week's lesson objectives in pupil-friendly language from the core goals and the group plan; code checks each maps to a goal code, and the teacher edits. The objectives flow onto the lesson slide template in the lesson tool ({LMS}). Adapting objectives to each student and explaining them in class stay with the teacher. No student names or support needs go into the drafting step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives were written lesson by lesson from the goals list.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson tools draft activities and text for a lesson goal.
tasks.still_hard: Students with disabilities need objectives that differ per student.
tasks.human_edge: Phrasing a goal so a student who has failed before believes they can reach it.
tasks.altitude: The teacher adapts and explains objectives instead of writing each from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether objectives are clear to assistants.

evidence.claim: Snappet lets AI draft a class activity for the lesson goal.
In a randomised trial with 259 science teachers in 68 English schools, ChatGPT plus a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with no quality difference.

assumptions: Boundary: from the group plan to objectives explained; lesson delivery is outside.
Input contract: core goals as a fixed list; group plan from the teacher; fallback is writing by hand.
Adapting and explaining do not change.
A DPIA under the school's privacy rules comes before use.
research_questions: How many drafted objectives does the teacher keep?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits the drafted objectives.

incremental.description: Special education teacher keeps the group plan in the tool current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: stable groups with known objectives; high: new groups and new units.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record attendance, behaviour and progress, keep group plans and scores, write report comments, prepare required reports, check the final reports, and send them to parents.

steps.what: Special education teacher maintains student records of attendance, behaviour and progress
Special education teacher keeps group plans and score exports in spreadsheets
Special education teacher writes comments for reports on students

loop.input: The teacher's notes and the student's scores and goal status for the period.
loop.output: A draft report comment per student.
loop.check: Each statement must trace to a note or score in the record, or it is dropped; the teacher edits and approves every comment.
loop.stop: One draft per student; if the teacher rejects it, they write the comment.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template lists scores; parents need a short personal explanation.

steps.what: Special education teacher prepares reports required by law and district policy
Special education teacher checks the final reports
Special education teacher sends the reports to parents

tasks.design: Attendance, behaviour and progress notes go into the pupil record system ({OTHER}) with quick-entry lists, and it shows goal status and scores per student, replacing spreadsheet group plans. Required reports are a query plus template. A bounded step drafts each report comment from the teacher's notes and scores; every statement must trace to the record, and the teacher edits. Once checked, reports go to parents through the parent app. No software sets marks or levels.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scores were exported to spreadsheets and every comment typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil record systems track goals and scores; language models draft comments from notes.
tasks.still_hard: Support needs are health data and need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Writing to parents about a hard term without taking away hope.
tasks.altitude: The teacher checks and edits instead of compiling and typing.

reach.learn: Whether records are complete at review time.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records, a development plan module and learning-goal tracking, with a parent app.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets education level is high-risk under Annex III point 3; here only comments are drafted and the teacher approves.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils have a say in pupil-data rules and staff consent to tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the school day to the reports sent; inspection visits are outside.
Input contract: records in the pupil system; templates set by the school; fallback is spreadsheets and typing.
Checking reports stays with the teacher.
A DPIA and the participation council's say come before use; support needs are not sent to the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted comments does the teacher change?

already_counted.description: Special education teacher edits drafted comments.

incremental.description: Special education teacher writes short notes during the term for the drafts.

approvals.approved_version: The reports as checked by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small class with short reports; high: many students and required reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The special education teacher keeps teaching, conferring with parents and deciding placements and plans; spreadsheets, scattered files and typed comments shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with more time for each student.
